title: Unawareness about data sharing implications
description: Homeowner registers without being fully aware of privacy implications of enrolling cameras and sensors, such as continuous monitoring data collection.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate based on general LINDDUN knowledge.

title: Disclosure of personal and device data in transit
description: Registration data including personal info and sensor details may be disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission to the Home Hub.

title: Linkability of homeowner to specific devices
description: The Home Hub can link the homeowner's identity to the enrolled cameras and sensors, enabling profiling of activities.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain about exact tree node for this scenario.

title: Unawareness of data processing
description: Guest user enters temporary access code without realizing the Home Hub may log or process this action in ways that track presence or associate with other data.
assumptions: Temporary code entry triggers logging at the hub.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate based on standard LINDDUN categories since no reference tree provided.

title: Detectability of access attempt
description: The act of transmitting/entering the access code over the flow could be observed by nearby parties, revealing that a guest is unlocking the door.
assumptions: Physical or side-channel observation of code entry.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate; may relate to meta-data exposure in transit.

title: Linkability via access logs
description: Home Hub may link the temporary code usage to specific times, other users, or events, enabling profiling of guest visits.
assumptions: Logs are kept and correlated internally.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate without exact Pro tree.

title: Non-repudiation of presence
description: Successful code entry creates irrefutable evidence in the system that the guest was at the location at a certain time.

title: Linkability of sensor events
description: Motion/door/sensor events written to local log can be linked over time to profile user presence, routines, and activities within the home.
assumptions: Events include timestamps and sensor IDs allowing correlation.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate based on typical LINDDUN Pro linkability subtrees for data storage; no reference material used.

title: Disclosure via log access
description: Stored events in the local event log may disclose sensitive home activity information if the datastore is accessed by unauthorized parties or through misconfiguration.
assumptions: Local log has insufficient access controls.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate; typical for information disclosure in storage.

title: Unawareness of logging
description: Home Hub writes events without ensuring users are aware of or have consented to the detailed logging of their sensor activities.
assumptions: No user notification or consent mechanism for local logging.

title: Detectability of camera clip uploads
description: An adversary observing network traffic can detect when the Home Hub uploads recorded clips to cloud storage, revealing patterns of home activity or occupancy.

title: Eavesdropping on video content in transit
description: If the upload channel is not properly encrypted, sensitive video clips containing identifiable individuals or private home scenes could be disclosed to interceptors.

title: Identifiable video storage without minimization
description: Cloud storage retains full video clips that identify residents, visitors, or activities, enabling long-term profiling if access controls or retention policies are weak.

title: User unawareness of clip sharing
description: Homeowners may be unaware that specific recorded clips are being uploaded and stored in the cloud, or of the privacy implications and third-party access possibilities.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate; typical for unawareness of data sharing in LINDDUN trees.

title: Potential non-compliance with data protection regulations
description: Storing biometric or identifiable video data in the cloud without explicit consent mechanisms, purpose limitation, or easy deletion options may violate GDPR/CCPA.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best guess without reference material; fits non-compliance category.

title: Linkability via flow metadata
description: Metadata about the real-time motion alert flow (timing, frequency, parties) can link the Home Hub to specific user identities or activity patterns.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate without reference material; based on typical LINDDUN linkability of data flows via metadata.

title: Disclosure of personal motion data
description: Mobile App Backend receives and may store/process real-time motion alerts revealing sensitive personal information about home occupancy and activities.

title: Unawareness of data sharing
description: Home Hub shares motion alerts without ensuring user awareness or consent for forwarding to backend.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate; threat arises from source's sharing act.

title: Excessive information in motion notification
description: Backend includes details about motion events in the push notification that may disclose sensitive home activity patterns to the homeowner or if intercepted.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate as no reference material provided.

title: Detectability of notifications revealing occupancy
description: The push notification flow's timing and existence can be detected, allowing inference about when the home has activity or is vacant.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate as no reference material provided.

title: Unawareness of notification data processing
description: Homeowner may be unaware of what personal data or inferences are derived from receiving and viewing the motion notifications on their device.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate as no reference material provided.

title: Unawareness of data sharing with third party
description: The mobile app backend shares aggregated analytics without ensuring end-users are fully aware of the sharing with the cloud analytics vendor.
assumptions: Users of the mobile app may not have been informed about backend analytics sharing.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate based on general LINDDUN knowledge without reference material.

title: Disclosure of analytics data by vendor
description: The cloud analytics vendor could further disclose or misuse the aggregated device-usage analytics received.
assumptions: Vendor may not have strict data handling policies.
uncertainty_note: Node id approximate; aggregation reduces but does not eliminate disclosure risks.

title: Linkability through flow metadata
description: Metadata about the data flow between backend and vendor could enable linking of the mobile service to specific analytics processing.
assumptions: Network observers or the vendor could use timing or volume metadata.
uncertainty_note: Low relevance for aggregated analytics; node id approximate.

title: Disclosure of personal video content in transit
description: Video clip containing identifiable homeowner activities or faces is retrieved from cloud storage to backend over the network, risking unauthorized disclosure if transmission lacks encryption or access controls.
assumptions: Video data qualifies as personal data under privacy regs; transmission occurs over potentially insecure channels without end-to-end protection.
uncertainty_note: Tree node Dd.1.1 is a best guess from general LINDDUN knowledge for disclosure during data flow; exact node may vary without reference material.

title: Unawareness about secondary processing of retrieved video
description: The mobile app backend receives the video clip for playback but may log, analyze, or retain it beyond the homeowner's knowledge or consent, leading to unawareness of data handling.
assumptions: Backend may perform additional processing like caching or analytics not explicitly disclosed to users.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain on exact tree node U.2.1 without LINDDUN Pro reference; applies if unawareness stems from lack of transparency at recipient.
